$meta.title: BASIC keyword examples
$meta.description: Hand-authored, machine-checked. Unlike its siblings in this directory this file is NOT generated: what a keyword is for, and the shortest example worth printing, are writing decisions. Everything factual about them is still checked — scripts/verify-samples.mjs types every `example` into the emulator and asserts every line of `output` verbatim, so the reference cannot print output the machine does not produce.

schema.syntax: The form the reference prints. Corrects the BIOS README where the README is wrong — see ACCURACY.md A20-A26.
schema.example: Lines to type. A block starting with a line number is typed in and RUN; anything else runs as it is entered.
schema.result: Prose, used instead of `output` when the result is real but not fixed (a clock, a random number).
schema.expect: Extra regexes, for the not-fixed cases.
schema.screen: Regexes matched against the screen — implies console video.
schema.sends: Input sent after the example, for the ones that ask a question.

PRINT.summary: Show numbers and text. `;` joins items tightly, `,` moves to the next 14-column zone, and a trailing `;` or `,` holds the cursor on the line.

LET.summary: Give a variable a value. `LET` is optional and almost nobody types it.

REM.summary: A remark. Everything after `REM` on the line is for people, not the machine.

END.summary: Stop the program and return to the prompt. Variables keep their values.

STOP.summary: Pause the program and say where it stopped. `CONT` picks it up again.

CONT.summary: Carry on from a `STOP` or a stopped program, at the line after the one it stopped on. Editing any line first makes it impossible.

RUN.summary: Run the program from the top, or from a line number if you give one. Clears the variables first.

LIST.summary: Show the program you have. It takes no line number — `LIST` lists the lot.

NEW.summary: Throw the program away and clear the variables. There is no undo.
NEW.result: 30718 bytes free — the same as a machine that has just been switched on, because the program is gone.

CLR.summary: Clear the variables, arrays and strings but keep the program.

GOTO.summary: Jump to a line and carry on from there.

GOSUB.summary: Jump to a subroutine, remembering where you came from. `RETURN` comes back.

RETURN.summary: Go back to the line after the `GOSUB` that called this subroutine.

ON.syntax: ON expr GOTO l1 [,l2 ...]   |   ON expr GOSUB l1 [,l2 ...]
ON.summary: Pick a destination by number: 1 takes the first line in the list, 2 the second. Out of range falls through to the next line.

IF.summary: Do something only when a test holds. `THEN 100` is short for `THEN GOTO 100`.
example: 20 IF A > 5 THEN PRINT "BIG" ELSE PRINT "SMALL"

THEN.summary: The part of `IF` that says what to do when the test holds.

ELSE.syntax: IF expr THEN stmt ELSE stmt
ELSE.summary: What to do when the test does not hold.

FOR.syntax: FOR var = start TO limit [STEP step]
FOR.summary: Count from one number to another, running everything up to `NEXT` each time round.
example: 20 PRINT N; " SQUARED IS"; N * N

NEXT.summary: End of a loop: add the step and go round again. One variable only — `NEXT J, I` is not accepted, so close each loop with its own `NEXT`.

TO.summary: The part of `FOR` that says where to count to.

STEP.syntax: FOR var = start TO limit STEP step
STEP.summary: How much to add each time round. Negative counts down.

DIM.summary: Make an array. One dimension only, and you get elements `0` to `size` — so `DIM S(9)` is ten of them.

DATA.summary: A list of values baked into the program for `READ` to work through. Skipped when the program runs past it.

READ.summary: Take the next value from the `DATA` lists and put it in a variable.

RESTORE.summary: Go back to the first `DATA` item, so you can read the list again.

FN.summary: Call a function you defined with `DEF`.

INPUT.summary: Stop and wait for the person at the keyboard to type something. Only works inside a program.

AND.summary: True when both sides are true — and, underneath, a bit-by-bit AND of two whole numbers.

OR.summary: True when either side is true — and, underneath, a bit-by-bit OR.

NOT.summary: Flips every bit, which turns true (`-1`) into false (`0`) — but `NOT 1` is `-2`, not `0`, so use it on comparisons rather than on counts.

TAB.summary: Inside `PRINT`, move to column `n` of the line.

SPC.summary: Inside `PRINT`, print `n` spaces from wherever the cursor is.

POS.summary: Which column the cursor is on. The argument is ignored; give it `0`.

SGN.summary: `-1` for a negative number, `0` for zero, `1` for a positive one.

INT.summary: Round down to a whole number — down towards minus infinity, so `INT(-3.7)` is `-4`.

ABS.summary: The size of a number, ignoring its sign.

RND.summary: A random number from 0 up to (but not including) 1. A negative argument reseeds from that number, so the same seed replays the same sequence.
RND.result: Three dice rolls, each from 1 to 6.

SIN.summary: Sine of an angle in radians.

COS.summary: Cosine of an angle in radians.

TAN.summary: Tangent of an angle in radians.

ATN.summary: Arctangent, in radians. `ATN(1) * 4` is a serviceable π.

HEX.summary: A number written in hexadecimal, always four digits with a `$` in front. `n` is 0 to 65535.

FRE.summary: How many bytes are left for variables, arrays and strings. The argument is ignored.

LEN.summary: How many characters are in a string.

LEFT$.summary: The first `n` characters of a string.

RIGHT$.summary: The last `n` characters of a string.

MID$.summary: Characters from the middle of a string, counting from 1. Leave `len` out to take the rest.

ASC.summary: The code of the first character of a string.

STR$.summary: A number turned into a string — keeping the leading space that `PRINT` puts where a minus sign would go.

VAL.summary: A string turned into a number. Reads as far as it can and gives `0` if that is nowhere.

PEEK.summary: Read one byte of memory, 0 to 255.
PEEK.result: The byte at address 781 — the machine's record of which cards are fitted.

POKE.summary: Write one byte of memory. `value` is 0 to 255.

SYS.summary: Call machine code at an address and come back when it returns.

WAIT.summary: Hold the program until reading `addr` and ANDing it with `mask` gives something other than zero. Nothing else happens while it waits.

BANK.summary: Choose which bank of extra RAM appears in the window at 32768.

MEM.summary: Print free memory, which cards the machine found, and the current disk. A statement, not a function — `PRINT MEM` is a syntax error.
MEM.result: Free bytes, the fitted-hardware byte, and the selected disk.

BRK.summary: Drop into the machine-code Monitor. `X` at the Monitor's `.` prompt comes back to BASIC.
BRK.result: The Monitor starts and shows the registers.

PAUSE.summary: Do nothing for `n` hundredths of a second.

CLS.summary: Clear the screen and put the cursor at the top left.

LOCATE.summary: Put the cursor somewhere. Rows are 0 to 23 down the screen, columns 0 to 39 across.

COLOR.summary: Set the text and background colours, each 0 to 15, for everything printed from now on.

SOUND.summary: Play a note: `voice` 1 to 3, `freq` in hertz, `dur` in hundredths of a second. The program waits for the note to finish.
SOUND.result: Three notes — the bottom of a C major chord.

JOY.summary: Read joystick 1 or 2. The bits are **active low** — a bit that reads `0` is a direction being pushed, so test with `= 0`, not with `<> 0`.
JOY.result: 255 with nothing being pushed: every bit high.

INKEY.summary: The code of a key being pressed right now, or `0` if none. Does not wait — put it in a loop.

TIME.summary: Print the time of day from the battery-backed clock.

DATE.summary: Print today's date from the battery-backed clock.

SETTIME.summary: Set the clock. It keeps running with the power off.
SETTIME.result: The clock now reads half past twelve.

SETDATE.summary: Set the date: century, year within it, month, day. 2026 is `20, 26`.

NVRAM.summary: 256 bytes of memory on the clock card that survive a power cut. A statement to write one, a function to read one.

DIR.summary: List the files on the current disk, with their sizes in bytes.

SAVE.summary: Write the program to the card. Bare `SAVE` sends it over the serial port instead, by XModem.

LOAD.summary: Read a program back off the card, replacing whatever is in memory. Bare `LOAD` receives one over the serial port by XModem.

DEL.summary: Delete a file from the current disk.

DISK.summary: Choose which of the card's 256 one-megabyte disks to work with.

FORMAT.summary: Erase the current disk and start it fresh. Asks first.

BSAVE.summary: Write raw bytes straight from memory to a file — a high score, a screen, a level.

BLOAD.summary: Read a file of raw bytes straight back into memory.
